_comment: Which Course Studio this repository expects. Under ADR-0005 the studio is a
sibling application built from our own fork, so this file names three things:
the fork commit our work sits on, the upstream commit it is level with, and
the image digest a deploy actually pulls.
The digest is the one that matters at deploy time. A commit says what the
source was; only a digest says what ran. `image.digest` is null until the
first image is published — a deploy must not proceed on a null.
Updating the studio is a decision, not a surprise: check_openmaic_contract.py
compares a checkout's HEAD against `commit` and reports the distance. It
reports; it does not force the move. Every rebase carries the DDL-drift risk
in OPENMAIC_INTEGRATION_V2_handoff.md §3.9, so bump `commit` and `verified`
only after a green pass — pg_dump, rebase, contract check, CI both sides.
`commit`/`commit_short`/`commit_date`/`verified`/`verified_against.locale_keys_en_us`
are read by check_openmaic_contract.py. Do not rename them without changing it.

fork.note: Not a fork on GitHub, on purpose: a repository GitHub classes as a fork does not run Actions until someone enables them by hand, and upstream's workflow triggers name upstream's branches. khunmax2/OpenMAIC (the original fork) is kept read-only for its pull request pages; every commit here descends from THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC's real history, and the `upstream` remote is how a rebase reaches it.

upstream.note: fork/main descends from upstream 29735f10 with 38 fork commits on top (base path, identity, Thai, embed, brand, TTS voices, raw PCM, image probe, libvips, /app/data, OpenAI-compatible image provider) as of 2026-09-11

image.note: phase 1 has not built one yet. A deploy must refuse a null digest rather than resolve a tag.

verified_against.upstream_gate: node scripts/check-i18n-keys.mjs — exact key alignment across the locale files

_comment: The name both sides must agree on. The gatekeeper sets it; the studio
reads it and turns it into an owner_id. Nothing else couples them.
A silent rename is the quietest failure this design has: no error, no
log line, the app keeps working, and every reader stops seeing their own
documents because the studio falls back to minting an anonymous owner
per browser. Pinning the name here is what turns that into a red check.
contract.studio_threaded_note: The fork threads authenticatedOwnerId as of 91b7423f, so the studio half of the identity assertion is a real check rather than a SKIP: something under lib/ must mention the header name, or the two sides have drifted apart.
contract.base_path_note: The path the studio image was BUILT to serve under. NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDIO_BASE_PATH is compiled in, so this is a property of the image, not of the deployment. The compose overlay's STUDIO_BASE_PATH only builds the healthcheck URL and must equal this value: if they drift, the healthcheck probes a path the image does not serve, the container never reports healthy, and nothing says why. It sits under DeepWitya's own base path on purpose: nginx picks the longest matching prefix, so `location /deepwitya/studio/` wins over `location /deepwitya/` without touching a rule that belongs to another team. It is NOT /deepwitya/course-studio, which is already taken -- that is DeepWitya's own page, the one holding the iframe. And it is /deepwitya, not the /deepwitya2 the second stack is validated under: that stack is shut down at cutover, and DeepWitya's own NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH is baked the same way, so both images are rebuilt together at that moment anyway.
contract.persistence_note: NEXT_PUBLIC_PERSISTENCE, compiled into the browser bundle. Without it the browser keeps everything locally and never calls the persistence API, so every per-account isolation property this deployment has stops being exercised -- silently, with no error and a studio that looks like it works. It is a build argument, so nothing in the running system can be asked whether it was passed; deploy/build-studio.sh passes it and the contract check asserts that script and this file still agree.
